topic.title: Scalable Inference for Structured Gaussian Processes
topic.area: Continuous Models and Scientific Machine Learning
topic.overview: Gaussian processes provide distributions over functions, but exact inference can become expensive or intractable in large or complex models. This cluster develops sparse representations, variational approximations, deep constructions, and multi-output dependencies. A representative black-box variational approach estimates objectives efficiently while allowing likelihoods that would otherwise require specialized inference derivations.
topic.whyItMatters: Approximation determines whether a probabilistic model remains useful at realistic scale. Saving computation should be assessed alongside retained dependencies and predictive uncertainty, especially when many outputs or hierarchical layers interact.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives develop sparse Gaussian processes and dynamical applications. Later work automates variational inference and challenges restrictive mean-field assumptions. Recent methods combine neural embeddings, inducing-kernel approximations, and stochastic inference to handle richer random fields or very large output spaces.
openQuestions: How can approximation error be diagnosed separately from a poorly chosen kernel?
Which scalable constructions retain calibrated uncertainty when outputs or inputs move beyond the training distribution?
